# Business Development Manager

## Hiring a BDM can be a game-changing move, especially if you’re the founder or agency owner who:

- 
**Dislikes sales or avoids it** because it feels pushy, uncomfortable, or “not your zone of genius”

- 
**Is stuck in fulfillment and delivery**, leaving little time to build the pipeline

- 
**Is growing through referrals and inbound leads**, but has no proactive strategy in place

- 
**Wants to scale beyond word-of-mouth**, but feels unsure how to create consistent deal flow

### 

![image](https://assets-v2.circle.so/dxfvhz6vecipds2j4y1mi9zii5ii)

### **Reframing Sales for Agency Owners Who Dislike It**

Many agency founders have a negative association with “sales” — often thinking of it as pushy, transactional, or manipulative. But **business development done well is not about forcing a sale** — it’s about:

- 
**Solving real problems for the right people**

- 
**Creating win-win outcomes**

- 
**Building long-term relationships**

- 
**Educating and guiding prospects to clarity**

Hiring a great BDM means you no longer have to:

- 
Send cold outreach messages

- 
Take every sales call yourself

- 
Chase leads who ghost

- 
Navigate awkward pricing conversations

Instead, you can focus on **vision, delivery, content, partnerships, or IP creation** — while your BDM drives pipeline, follows up, and closes deals aligned with your values.

### **Before You Hire: Make Sure These Are in Place**

- 
✅ A clear offer with proven results

- 
✅ Defined pricing and deliverables

- 
✅ Basic sales assets (case studies, pitch deck, CRM, etc.)

- 
✅ Willingness to invest in training/onboarding the BDM (especially if they’re new to your niche)

- 
✅ A clear handoff process from lead → proposal → client**Core Responsibilities:**

- 
Identify and develop new business opportunities

- 
Build and maintain relationships with key clients

- 
Collaborate with marketing and product teams

- 
Negotiate and close business deals

- 
Track metrics and report performance

**Typical KPIs:**

- 
Number of qualified leads generated

- 
Deals closed / revenue generated

- 
Sales pipeline value and velocity

- 
Client retention or expansion rates

- 
Market expansion success

**Key Outcomes You Expect:**

- 
Increased revenue and profitability

- 
Strong pipeline of qualified opportunities

- 
Expansion into new markets or verticals

- 
Long-term partnerships and client relationships

title: Leveraging AI for Research
body:
# Leveraging AI for Research

## 1. Analyze the Competitive Landscape

**Prompt:**
“Analyze the competitive landscape for [Client Name or Industry]. Who are the top competitors? What are their key strengths and weaknesses in marketing, product, and customer experience?”

**Why this works:**
This prompt helps you get a broad overview of the competition, focusing on relevant details like brand positioning, product differentiators, and marketing strategy. You can specify “top 5 competitors” or refine it to certain aspects (e.g. social media, content marketing) depending on the client’s needs.

## 2. Identify White Space Opportunities

**Prompt:**
“Identify gaps or white space opportunities in the [Client’s Industry or Market Segment] that [Client Name] could target with new products, services, or marketing strategies. What unmet needs or underserved customer segments exist?”

**Why this works:**
This focuses the AI on discovering areas where the client can differentiate or innovate. You can also specify a region, demographic, or digital platform to tailor the analysis.

## 3. Assess Brand Positioning

**Prompt:**
“Evaluate [Client Name]’s current brand positioning compared to competitors. What are the key differentiators? Are there inconsistencies or missed opportunities in their messaging or marketing channels?”

**Why this works:**
This helps you understand how the brand is perceived in the market, where it’s strong, and where it might be vulnerable or inconsistent.

## 4. Evaluate Marketing Strategy Effectiveness

**Prompt:**
“Assess the effectiveness of [Client Name]’s current marketing strategy. How does it compare to competitors in terms of reach, engagement, and conversion? Are there any channels or tactics where competitors are outperforming them?”

**Why this works:**
This encourages the AI to benchmark the client’s marketing efforts (e.g. social media, SEO, paid ads, influencer marketing) against competitors and highlight any areas where the client is falling behind.

## 5. Recommend Strategic Improvements

**Prompt:**
“Based on the competitive landscape and [Client Name]’s current strategy, recommend 3-5 strategic improvements they could make to strengthen their market position and grow their business.”

**Why this works:**
This prompt drives actionable insights. You can even specify the focus (e.g. product development, branding, customer experience) to match the client’s priorities.

## Bonus Tip: Combine or Chain Prompts

You can also **chain these prompts** together to create a deeper analysis pipeline. For example:
➡️ Start with prompt #1 to understand the competitive landscape.
➡️ Use prompt #3 to zero in on the client’s brand positioning relative to competitors.
➡️ Finish with prompt #5 to get strategic recommendations.

title: Customer Alignment (Reviews)
body:
# Customer Alignment (Reviews)

### Customer Alignment & The Power of Reviews

**What is Customer Alignment?**

Customer alignment means ensuring your messaging, offers, and service delivery meet the real needs, expectations, and language of your ideal customer. When you're aligned:

- 
Customers *feel understood*.

- 
Sales become smoother and faster.

- 
Retention and referrals go up.

**Why Reviews Matter for Customer Alignment**

Reviews are more than testimonials—they’re **live customer intelligence**.

**They tell you:**

- 
What your clients value most about you.

- 
What language they use to describe your impact.

- 
What problems they believe you solve best.

- 
Where there may be disconnects or unmet expectations.

### 🔑 **Key Reasons Reviews Are Critical**

1. **Clarity for Messaging**

Use phrases from real reviews to shape your website copy, sales pages, and pitch. It’s your customer's voice—use it.

2. **Trust & Proof**

Social proof is one of the strongest conversion tools. 93% of customers read reviews before buying. One strong review can do more than 1,000 words of copy.

3. **Feedback Loop**

Negative or neutral reviews reveal opportunities to fix gaps and re-align your delivery with what customers expect or want most.

4. **SEO Benefits**

Public reviews (Google, Yelp, etc.) boost your search visibility and relevance.

5. **Retention Signal**

Asking for reviews shows you value your customers’ opinions. It increases engagement and emotional investment.

### 💡 Review Mining for Alignment

**Step 1:** Collect 5-10 recent reviews from your client AND their competitors

**Step 2:** Highlight:

- 
The exact words/phrases customers use to describe results.

- 
Pain points mentioned 

- 
Unexpected wins or emotional breakthroughs they share.

**Step 3:** Use this insight to refine your:

- 
Offer positioning

- 
Sales scripts

- 
Onboarding process

### ✅ Takeaway

“If you’re not learning from your reviews, you’re leaving trust, clarity, and revenue on the table.”

title: The Brand Diagnostic Workshop

# The Brand Diagnostic Workshop

Access the Canva template here - [BRAND DIAGNOSTIC WORKSHOP](https://www.canva.com/design/DAGUnR2tgAg/YXi2MdxfXh8PcUgmYUX7gQ/view?utm_content=DAGUnR2tgAg&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link&utm_source=publishsharelink&mode=preview)

The workshop is an opportunity to ask the client questions about their brand, their goals and to start to build a lasting relationship. 

Dig deep, keep asking questions until you get answers. 

**Build rapport** - spend the first few minutes on a personal level. 

**Goals** - Understand their financial goals, and where they are at now in comparison to those goals. 

**Obstacles** - Why have they not reached these goals previously? What was in their way? What obstacles are there in the future that may stop them from reaching these goals? 

**Customer Personas - **Build the customer profiles and list the demographics (age, gender, income, family size) psychographic (brands they purchase, cultural values).

**Pains** - Dig deep into the real pain here. For example, someone may have a skin issue such as discolouration, but the real pain for them is not liking how they look or not feeling beautiful.

**Dream Outcome:** This is aligned to the pain above - if the pain is not liking how they look their dream outcome is to have clear skin and feel beautiful

**Objections: **List anything that may stop them from making a purchase. This will be things like trusting the brand, the product not being delivered quickly enough, the price being higher than competitors. This will be key to driving messaging.

**Product/Offers: **What offers do they have permanently and ad hoc? What has worked in the past? What are they willing or able to offer?

title: Gap Analysis
body:
# Gap Analysis

The Gap Analysis is the heart of the Momentum Map. It shows the client where they are now, where they want to go, and what’s missing in between.
But the power lies in **what you prioritize**: not everything, but **what moves the needle fastest**.

By focusing on **low-hanging fruit**, you help your client:

- 
See immediate value in your insight

- 
Build trust through early wins

- 
Buy into a longer-term strategy because they’ve experienced fast traction

### 🧩 **What to Include in the Gap Analysis**

Break down the client’s business across key areas (e.g., offer, pricing, funnel, visibility, lead flow, systems, delivery). For each area:

- 
Identify what’s working

- 
Surface what’s missing

- 
Prioritize what’s easy to fix and has high impact

Use simple scoring (e.g., Red / Yellow / Green) or a snapshot matrix to make gaps visual and digestible.

### ⚡ **Focus: Quick Wins / Low-Hanging Fruit**

These are:

- 
High-impact, low-effort actions

- 
Things the client already has but isn’t using fully

- 
Small tweaks that drive momentum (e.g., clearer CTA, faster lead follow-up, tighter messaging, email revival)

You're not just showing what’s wrong—you’re showing what’s *ready to work now*.

🗣️ **How to Present It**

Frame the Gap Analysis as an **opportunity map**, not a critique.
Lead with the quick wins to build buy-in:

“Here are the areas where we can make simple moves now that will unlock the biggest results fastest.”

Then, position the rest as part of a longer-term roadmap that your services or strategy can support.

### ✅ **Outcome for Your Client**

- 
Clarity on where they’re stuck

- 
Excitement about what’s possible

- 
Confidence in *you* as the expert who sees the whole picture and knows where to start

Including a product-market fit graph in a brand diagnostic assessment provides a clear visual representation of how well a product or service meets the needs of its target audience.

title: What is the low hagning fruit methodology?
body:
# What is the low hagning fruit methodology?

### 🧠 The Core Principle

Most marketing strategies fail to create momentum because they start with **big, complex, long-term plays** (like content funnels, SEO, brand building) that take **months to yield results**.

Meanwhile, business owners are often cash-strapped, stressed, and need traction *now*.

**The Low Hanging Fruit Methodology flips that script.**
It focuses on identifying and executing **quick wins** that can:

- 
Bring in fast cash

- 
Build confidence

- 
Prove offer-market fit

- 
Create momentum for longer-term strategies

### 🚀 Why It Works

- 
**Money loves momentum.** Getting early wins creates confidence, cash flow, and buy-in.

- 
**Faster feedback loops.** You learn what works with real-time data.

- 
**Lower resistance.** It’s easier to execute and requires fewer resources.

- 
**De-risks the strategy.** You fund long-term plays *with short-term wins.*

**Product/Offers: **What offers do they have permanently and ad hoc? What has worked in the past? What are they willing or able to offer?

**Competitors:** You will be looking at this in the historical analysis but asking a client who they think their competitors are is important. 

**Cold Acquisition:** How are they currently attracting new customers, do they offer anything to bring customers/clients into their email list?

title: Product Market Fit Stage
body:
# Product Market Fit Stage

Including a product-market fit graph in a brand diagnostic assessment provides a clear visual representation of how well a product or service meets the needs of its target audience.

This graph highlights areas where the brand sits in terms of scale and is based on customer engagement (positive reviews), list size, current roas and social media growth. 

A client would not be ready to scale until they have identified and met a genuine demand, leading to strong customer satisfaction, loyalty, and organic growth.

title: Customer Alignment (Reviews)
body:
# Customer Alignment (Reviews)

### Customer Alignment & The Power of Reviews

**What is Customer Alignment?**

Customer alignment means ensuring your messaging, offers, and service delivery meet the real needs, expectations, and language of your ideal customer. When you're aligned:

- 
Customers *feel understood*.

- 
Sales become smoother and faster.

- 
Retention and referrals go up.

**Why Reviews Matter for Customer Alignment**

Reviews are more than testimonials—they’re **live customer intelligence**.

**They tell you:**

- 
What your clients value most about you.

- 
What language they use to describe your impact.

- 
What problems they believe you solve best.

- 
Where there may be disconnects or unmet expectations.

### 🔑 **Key Reasons Reviews Are Critical**

1. **Clarity for Messaging**

Use phrases from real reviews to shape your website copy, sales pages, and pitch. It’s your customer's voice—use it.

2. **Trust & Proof**

Social proof is one of the strongest conversion tools. 93% of customers read reviews before buying. One strong review can do more than 1,000 words of copy.

3. **Feedback Loop**

Negative or neutral reviews reveal opportunities to fix gaps and re-align your delivery with what customers expect or want most.

4. **SEO Benefits**

Public reviews (Google, Yelp, etc.) boost your search visibility and relevance.

5. **Retention Signal**

Asking for reviews shows you value your customers’ opinions. It increases engagement and emotional investment.

### 💡 Review Mining for Alignment

**Step 1:** Collect 5-10 recent reviews from your client AND their competitors

**Step 2:** Highlight:

- 
The exact words/phrases customers use to describe results.

- 
Pain points mentioned 

- 
Unexpected wins or emotional breakthroughs they share.

**Step 3:** Use this insight to refine your:

- 
Offer positioning

- 
Sales scripts

- 
Onboarding process

### ✅ Takeaway

“If you’re not learning from your reviews, you’re leaving trust, clarity, and revenue on the table.”

title: Gap Analysis
body:
# Gap Analysis

The Gap Analysis is the heart of the Momentum Map. It shows the client where they are now, where they want to go, and what’s missing in between.
But the power lies in **what you prioritize**: not everything, but **what moves the needle fastest**.

By focusing on **low-hanging fruit**, you help your client:

- 
See immediate value in your insight

- 
Build trust through early wins

- 
Buy into a longer-term strategy because they’ve experienced fast traction

### 🧩 **What to Include in the Gap Analysis**

Break down the client’s business across key areas (e.g., offer, pricing, funnel, visibility, lead flow, systems, delivery). For each area:

- 
Identify what’s working

- 
Surface what’s missing

- 
Prioritize what’s easy to fix and has high impact

Use simple scoring (e.g., Red / Yellow / Green) or a snapshot matrix to make gaps visual and digestible.

### ⚡ **Focus: Quick Wins / Low-Hanging Fruit**

These are:

- 
High-impact, low-effort actions

- 
Things the client already has but isn’t using fully

- 
Small tweaks that drive momentum (e.g., clearer CTA, faster lead follow-up, tighter messaging, email revival)

You're not just showing what’s wrong—you’re showing what’s *ready to work now*.

🗣️ **How to Present It**

Frame the Gap Analysis as an **opportunity map**, not a critique.
Lead with the quick wins to build buy-in:

“Here are the areas where we can make simple moves now that will unlock the biggest results fastest.”

Then, position the rest as part of a longer-term roadmap that your services or strategy can support.

### ✅ **Outcome for Your Client**

- 
Clarity on where they’re stuck

- 
Excitement about what’s possible

- 
Confidence in *you* as the expert who sees the whole picture and knows where to start

title: Leveraging AI for Research
body:
# Leveraging AI for Research

## 1. Analyze the Competitive Landscape

**Prompt:**
“Analyze the competitive landscape for [Client Name or Industry]. Who are the top competitors? What are their key strengths and weaknesses in marketing, product, and customer experience?”

**Why this works:**
This prompt helps you get a broad overview of the competition, focusing on relevant details like brand positioning, product differentiators, and marketing strategy. You can specify “top 5 competitors” or refine it to certain aspects (e.g. social media, content marketing) depending on the client’s needs.

## 2. Identify White Space Opportunities

**Prompt:**
“Identify gaps or white space opportunities in the [Client’s Industry or Market Segment] that [Client Name] could target with new products, services, or marketing strategies. What unmet needs or underserved customer segments exist?”

**Why this works:**
This focuses the AI on discovering areas where the client can differentiate or innovate. You can also specify a region, demographic, or digital platform to tailor the analysis.

## 3. Assess Brand Positioning

**Prompt:**
“Evaluate [Client Name]’s current brand positioning compared to competitors. What are the key differentiators? Are there inconsistencies or missed opportunities in their messaging or marketing channels?”

**Why this works:**
This helps you understand how the brand is perceived in the market, where it’s strong, and where it might be vulnerable or inconsistent.

## 4. Evaluate Marketing Strategy Effectiveness

**Prompt:**
“Assess the effectiveness of [Client Name]’s current marketing strategy. How does it compare to competitors in terms of reach, engagement, and conversion? Are there any channels or tactics where competitors are outperforming them?”

**Why this works:**
This encourages the AI to benchmark the client’s marketing efforts (e.g. social media, SEO, paid ads, influencer marketing) against competitors and highlight any areas where the client is falling behind.

## 5. Recommend Strategic Improvements

**Prompt:**
“Based on the competitive landscape and [Client Name]’s current strategy, recommend 3-5 strategic improvements they could make to strengthen their market position and grow their business.”

**Why this works:**
This prompt drives actionable insights. You can even specify the focus (e.g. product development, branding, customer experience) to match the client’s priorities.

## Bonus Tip: Combine or Chain Prompts

You can also **chain these prompts** together to create a deeper analysis pipeline. For example:
➡️ Start with prompt #1 to understand the competitive landscape.
➡️ Use prompt #3 to zero in on the client’s brand positioning relative to competitors.
➡️ Finish with prompt #5 to get strategic recommendations.

# Understanding your Client Acquisition Numbers

👉 TOOL: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1i15syvn8uumtzkC2wMrQ021JCEyGDUpNMfDW032KI6g/copy?gid=0#gid=0](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1i15syvn8uumtzkC2wMrQ021JCEyGDUpNMfDW032KI6g/copy?gid=0#gid=0)

**Client Acquisition Reporting (Foundations First)**

Client acquisition reporting is about understanding the *numbers behind your growth*, not building or optimising funnels yet. At this stage, we are not going deep into funnel strategy or execution. That work comes later, typically weeks 4–7.

Right now, this is your opportunity to get familiar with the core metrics that drive client growth: how many leads you need, how many conversations that turns into, and what it realistically takes to acquire the number of clients you’ve outlined in your $10k plan.

This early reporting builds clarity and confidence. Instead of guessing or relying on hope, you start to see the relationship between activity, conversion, and revenue. That context makes the later funnel work far more effective because you already understand what “enough” looks like for your business.

Think of this as learning the language of growth. We are laying the numerical foundation now, so when we optimise acquisition later, you’re making decisions from data rather than pressure or overwhelm.

title: Working with Appointment Setters
body:
# Working with Appointment Setters

## Best Places to Find Appointment Setters

### 1. LinkedIn (Highest quality for B2B)

Best if you want someone who understands business conversations, not just scripts.

Where to look:

- 
Search job titles like:

- 
Appointment Setter

- 
Sales Development Representative (SDR)

- 
Business Development Representative (BDR)

- 
Outbound Sales Assistant

- 
Post directly on your company page

- 
Use LinkedIn Jobs with clear expectations

Best for:

- 
Strategy-led agencies

- 
Ecommerce growth agencies

- 
Higher-value services

- 
Outbound via LinkedIn and email

Watch out for:

- 
Corporate-only sellers who expect heavy structure

- 
People who avoid outbound entirely

### 2. [OnlineJobs.ph](http://onlinejobs.ph/) (Strong value, very common for agencies)

One of the most popular platforms for appointment setters, especially from the Philippines.

Why it works:

- 
Large pool of experienced setters

- 
Many already trained in cold outreach

- 
Cost-effective

- 
Easy to test quickly

Best for:

- 
LinkedIn and email outreach

- 
Volume-based prospecting

- 
Agencies with clear scripts and ICPs

Watch out for:

- 
You must train and manage well

- 
Skill levels vary a lot

### 3. Upwork (Best for testing fast)

Good if you want to trial before committing to a hire.

How to use it well:

- 
Search “appointment setter B2B” or “SDR outbound”

- 
Look for people with agency or ecommerce experience

- 
Start with a paid trial week

Best for:

- 
Short-term tests

- 
Building SOPs

- 
Proving outbound works before hiring

Watch out for:

- 
Higher hourly rates for strong talent

- 
Some freelancers juggle multiple clients

### 4. Sales-Specific Communities

Underrated and often higher quality.

Where to look:

- 
SDR and sales Slack communities

- 
Founder and agency Facebook groups

- 
Paid sales communities and masterminds

Best for:

- 
Referrals

- 
People who already understand modern outbound

- 
Culture-aligned hires

### 5. Recruitment Agencies (Higher cost, less hands-on)

Useful if you want someone more senior.

Best for:

- 
Experienced SDRs

- 
Salespeople who can help design outbound

- 
Less training required

Trade-off:

- 
Higher salary expectations

- 
Less flexible

## What to Look For in an Appointment Setter

Regardless of platform, screen for:

- 
Clear written communication

- 
Comfort starting conversations

- 
Ability to follow a process

- 
Curiosity and listening skills

- 
Experience with LinkedIn or email outreach

- 
Understanding of B2B or ecommerce buyers

Red flags:

- 
Script-only mindset

- 
Obsession with volume over quality

- 
No questions about the offer or ICP

## Typical Setup That Works Best

For agencies like yours:

- 
Appointment setter handles:

- 
Lead sourcing

- 
Initial outreach

- 
Follow-ups

- 
Booking calls

- 
Sales consultant handles:

- 
Discovery

- 
Pitch

- 
Closing

That split keeps quality high and burnout low.

📄 Moor Marketing Agency SOP: Staff Pay Cycles & Contractor Invoicing

## Purpose

To establish clear guidelines for processing weekly staff payments and managing fortnightly contractor invoicing, ensuring timely and accurate compensation for all personnel.

## Scope

This SOP applies to all full-time and part-time employees, as well as independent contractors engaged with Moor Marketing Agency.

## 1. Staff Pay Cycles

### 1.1 Payment Schedule

- 
**Frequency**: Weekly

- 
**Payment Day**: Every Monday

### 1.2 Processing Procedure

- 
**Timesheet Submission**: Employees must submit completed timesheets by 5:00 PM every Friday.

- 
**Review and Approval**: Supervisors will review and approve timesheets by 12:00 PM each Saturday.

- 
**Payroll Processing**: The finance team will process payroll on Monday to ensure payments are made on Monday.

### 1.3 Responsibilities

- 
**Employees**: Timely submission of accurate timesheets.

- 
**Supervisors**: Prompt review and approval of timesheets.

- 
**Finance Team**: Accurate and timely processing of payroll.

## 2. Contractor Invoicing

### 2.1 Invoicing Schedule

- 
**Frequency**: Fortnightly

- 
**Payment Days**: Every second Monday

### 2.2 Invoice Submission

- 
**Deadline**: Invoices must be received no later than one week prior to the scheduled payment Monday. For example, for payment on Monday, June 9, the invoice must be received by Monday, June 2.

- 
**Submission Method**: All invoices should be emailed to [accounts@moormarketing.com.au](mailto:accounts@moormarketing.com.au).

### 2.3 Invoice Requirements

Each invoice must include:

- 
**Contractor Details**: Full name, ABN, and contact information.

- 
**Invoice Number**: Unique identifier for tracking.

- 
**Invoice Date**: Date of issuance.

- 
**Description of Services**: Detailed breakdown of services provided, including dates and hours worked.

- 
**Total Amount Due**: Clearly stated in AUD.

- 
**Payment Terms**: As agreed upon in the contractor agreement.

### 2.4 Processing Procedure

- 
**Verification**: The finance team will verify the accuracy of the invoice details.

- 
**Approval**: Invoices will be approved by the relevant project manager.

- 
**Payment**: Approved invoices will be scheduled for payment on the next fortnightly cycle.

### 2.5 Late Submissions

- 
**Policy**: Invoices received after the submission deadline will be processed in the following payment cycle.

## 3. Record Keeping

- 
**Storage**: All payroll and invoice records will be securely stored in the company's financial management system (XERO).

- 
**Retention**: Records will be retained for a minimum of seven years in compliance with Australian taxation laws.

## 4. Contact Information

For any queries related to payroll or invoicing, please contact:

- 
**Finance Department**: [accounts@moormarketing.com.au](mailto:accounts@moormarketing.com.au)

# Team Onboarding

📘 Moor Marketing Agency SOP: Team Onboarding Process

## Purpose

To provide a structured and consistent onboarding experience for new team members, facilitating their integration into the company culture, tools, and workflows.

## Scope

This SOP applies to all new hires at Moor Marketing Agency, including full-time employees, part-time staff, and contractors.

## 1. Pre-Onboarding

### 1.1 Welcome Email

Upon acceptance of the job offer, the HR department sends a welcome email to the new hire, which includes:

- 
A warm welcome message.

- 
Start date and time.

- 
Overview of the onboarding schedule.

- 
List of tools and platforms to be used:

- 
Monday.com

- 
Slack

- 
Email (Gmail)

- 
LastPass

- 
SharePoint

- 
(Specific job access such as FB or Google)

- 
Contact information for Team Lead and the assigned buddy.

### 1.2 Account Setup

The team manager is responsible for setting up the following accounts and access:

- 
[**Monday.com**](http://Monday.com): Create user account and assign to relevant boards.

- 
**Slack**: Create user account and add to appropriate channels

- 
**Email**: Set up on company email 

- 
**LastPass**: Create user account and share necessary passwords.

- 
**SharePoint**: Grant access to relevant folders and documents.

All account credentials and access details are to be securely shared with the new hire via LastPass.

## 2. Onboarding Week

The first week consists of scheduled training sessions and introductions:

### 2.1 Day 1: Orientation

- 
Welcome meeting with Team Lead and the assigned buddy.

- 
Overview of company culture, mission, and values

- 
Introduction to company policies and procedures.

### 2.2 Days 2–5: Tool and Process Training

- 
[**Monday.com**](http://Monday.com): Task management and project tracking.

- 
**Slack**: Communication protocols and best practices.

- 
**Email**: Usage guidelines and etiquette.

- 
**LastPass**: Password management and security practices.

- 
**SharePoint**: Document storage and collaboration.

Each session includes hands-on training and Q&A segments.

## 3. Buddy Program

Each new hire is assigned a buddy for the first two weeks:

- 
**Role of the Buddy**:

- 
Provide guidance and support

- 
Answer questions and clarify

- 
Assist with integration into the team and company culture.

- 
**Interaction Schedule**:

- 
Daily check-ins during the first week

- 
Alternate-day check-ins during the second week.

## 4. Reporting Manager Assignment

A reporting manager is assigned to each new hire to:

- 
Set performance goals and expectations.

- 
Provide feedback and evaluations.

- 
Facilitate professional development and growth.

An initial meeting is scheduled during the onboarding week to establish communication channels and discuss objectives.

## 5. Post-Onboarding Review

At the end of the two-week onboarding period:

- 
HR conducts a feedback session with the new hire to assess the onboarding experience.

- 
The buddy and reporting manager provide input on the new hire's integration and performance.

- 
Any necessary adjustments or additional support are identified and implemented.

## 6. Documentation and Record-Keeping

All onboarding activities, including training sessions, meetings, and feedback, are documented and stored securely in SharePoint for future reference.

By adhering to this SOP, Moor Marketing Agency ensures a consistent and effective onboarding experience, setting new team members up for success from day one.

# Leave Requests

## 1. Leave Entitlements

### 1.1 Full-Time Employees

- 
**Annual Leave**: As per the National Employment Standards (NES), full-time employees are entitled to 20 days of paid annual leave per year.

- 
**Personal/Carer's Leave**: 10 days of paid personal/carer's leave per year.

- 
**Public Holidays**: Entitled to paid leave on public holidays observed in Victoria.

### 1.2 Part-Time Employees

- 
**Pro-Rated Leave**: Entitlements are calculated on a pro-rata basis according to hours worked.

- 
**Public Holidays**: Entitled to paid leave on public holidays if the day falls on a usual workday.

### 1.3 Contractors

- 
**Leave Entitlements**: As independent contractors, leave entitlements are governed by the terms specified in individual contracts.

- 
**Unpaid Leave**: Contractors may request unpaid leave, subject to managerial approval and contractual terms.

## 2. Leave Request Procedure

### 2.1 Submission

- 
**Notice Period**:

- 
**Annual Leave**: Submit requests at least 4 weeks in advance.

- 
**Personal/Carer's Leave**: Notify as soon as practicable, preferably before the start of the workday.

- 
**Method**: Submit leave requests through Monday.com leave request form

### 2.2 Approval Process

- 
**Manager Review**: Direct supervisors will review leave requests, considering team workload and staffing requirements.

- 
**Confirmation**: Your direct manager will confirm leave entitlements and update records accordingly.

### 2.3 Communication

- 
**Notification**: Employees will receive written confirmation of approved leave.

- 
**Calendar Updates**: Approved leave will be reflected in the team calendar to ensure transparency and planning.

## 3. Special Considerations

### 3.1 Unpaid Leave

- 
**Eligibility**: Employees may request unpaid leave for extended absences not covered by paid leave entitlements.

- 
**Approval**: Subject to managerial discretion and operational requirements.

### 3.2 Leave During Peak Periods

- 
**Restrictions**: Leave during peak operational periods may be limited. Employees are encouraged to plan accordingly.

## 4. Record Keeping

- 
**Documentation**: All leave requests and approvals will be documented and stored securely in Monday.com

- 
**Monitoring**: Accounts will monitor leave balances

## 5. Return to Work

- 
**Notification**: Employees are expected to confirm their return to work date prior to resuming duties.

- 
**Medical Clearance**: For extended personal or medical leave, a medical certificate may be required to confirm fitness for duty.

## 6. Non-Compliance

- 
**Unauthorized Absence**: Failure to follow the leave request procedure may result in the absence being recorded as unauthorized, potentially leading to disciplinary action.

## Purpose

To ensure all client projects and retainers are structured, budgeted, and tracked consistently using [Monday.com](http://Monday.com) for streamlined task visibility, workload prioritisation, and financial oversight.

## Scope

This SOP applies to all client retainers and one-off projects managed within the Moor Marketing Agency [Monday.com](http://Monday.com) workspace.

## 1. Board Setup

### 1.1 Use the Main Template

- 
All project and retainer boards must be created by **duplicating the approved main template**.

- 
The template includes pre-configured columns for:

- 
Task Item

- 
Owner

- 
Status

- 
Due Date

- 
Time Tracking

- 
Allocated Hours

- 
Rate Formula

- 
Task Budget

❗️Do not create boards from scratch to ensure uniformity and automation compatibility.

## 2. Task Creation

### 2.1 Task Input

- 
Each deliverable or work stream must be entered as a **separate task** under the correct monthly section (e.g., “June 2025”).

- 
Assign the **task owner** and **due date** immediately upon creation.

### 2.2 Allocated Hours & Budget

- 
Every task must have an **estimated time in hours** allocated.

- 
A formula in the board automatically multiplies hours by the hourly rate to calculate the **task-level budget**.

- 
The cumulative total of all tasks forms the **total retainer or project budget**.

## 3. Prioritisation & Workflow Automations

### 3.1 Automatic Task Addition to Priority Board

- 
Once a new task is entered into a project or retainer board, it will **automatically appear in the ‘PRIORITY BOARD’** via existing automations.

### 3.2 Re-adding Missed Tasks

- 
If a task doesn’t sync or needs to be manually re-added:

- 
Update the task **status column** (e.g., "Set to Active") to trigger the automation again.

### 3.3 Automation Rules

Boards include several automations such as:

- 
**Status-triggered alerts**

- 
**Date reminders for overdue tasks**

- 
**Sync to Priority Board**

- 
**Budget recalculations based on task updates**

🛠 Any changes to automation should be approved by the systems manager or project lead.

## 4. Time Tracking & Reporting

- 
Team members must **track time** against each task using the time tracking column in [Monday.com](http://Monday.com).

- 
Time logs are reviewed weekly for project budget reconciliation and team productivity analysis.

## 5. Board Structure & Navigation

- 
Each board is organized by **month**, allowing for clear segmentation of deliverables.

- 
Tasks are grouped under their respective months for easier planning and review.

- 
Additional views (e.g., Gantt, Dashboard, Kanban) are available for project managers to visualize timelines and progress.

## 6. Archiving & Maintenance

- 
At the end of each month, tasks should be reviewed, completed, or carried forward.

- 
Completed tasks are archived to reduce clutter.

- 
Project managers are responsible for keeping boards clean and up to date.

# Task Prioritisation

📋 SOP: Task Prioritisation Process

## Purpose

To ensure all team members are focused on the most impactful and time-sensitive work by maintaining a clear, centralized, and updated daily task priority list using [Monday.com](http://Monday.com).

## Scope

This SOP applies to all internal team members and contractors working on tasks across copywriting, design, strategy, advertising, and other functions.

## 1. System Overview

### 1.1 The Prioritisation Board

- 
A **dedicated **[**Monday.com**](http://Monday.com)** board** is used exclusively for task prioritisation.

- 
Tasks are pulled automatically from all client and project boards using **automations**.

- 
The board includes columns for:

- 
Task Name

- 
Source Project

- 
Assigned Team Member

- 
Department (e.g., Copywriting, Design, Strategy)

- 
Status

- 
Due Date

- 
Priority (Manually ordered)

### 1.2 Department Channels

- 
Upon entry, each task is routed to its appropriate department via automation rules:

- 
**Copywriting**

- 
**Design**

- 
**Strategy**

- 
**Client Services**

- 
**Ad Ops**

- 
This allows teams to quickly filter and focus on tasks relevant to their function.

## 2. Daily Prioritisation Workflow

### 2.1 Daily Morning Stand-Up

- 
The team gathers for a **daily prioritisation meeting** (typically 15–20 minutes).

- 
This meeting is led by the **Project Manager** or **Account Lead**.

### 2.2 Review of Tasks

During the meeting, the team:

- 
Reviews new tasks added since the previous day.

- 
Identifies critical, time-sensitive, or blocked tasks.

- 
Confirms owner and estimated time to complete.

### 2.3 Ordering Tasks

- 
Tasks in each department section are **manually reordered** to reflect their true priority for the day.

- 
The highest-priority tasks are moved to the top of each department group.

- 
If any task is *no longer relevant or needs to be postponed*, its status is updated accordingly.

⚠️ Important: **Only the Project Manager or Account Lead** should reorder tasks to maintain consistency.

## 3. Task Execution & Updates

### 3.1 During the Day

- 
Team members are expected to work through tasks **in the order presented** unless otherwise discussed.

- 
If they encounter blockers, they must communicate immediately in the relevant Slack channel or during midday huddles (if applicable).

### 3.2 Status Updates

- 
Team members must update the **status column** in real-time (e.g., “In Progress”, “Waiting for Review”, “Complete”).

- 
This allows managers to track progress and reallocate resources as needed.

## 4. Exceptions & Urgent Work

- 
If urgent work arises outside of the morning meeting:

- 
It must be discussed and approved by the **Project Manager**.

- 
The task should be added manually to the board and positioned appropriately in the department queue.

## 5. End-of-Day Clean-Up

- 
Each day, the Project Manager reviews tasks marked as complete and removes or archives them if fully resolved.

- 
Any leftover tasks are re-evaluated the next morning.

# Performance Management

📋 SOP: Managing Underperformance

## Purpose

To ensure performance concerns are addressed consistently, respectfully, and in compliance with fair work regulations. This process aims to support the team member in improving their performance through structured guidance, measurable expectations, and ongoing support.

## Scope

This SOP applies to all employees and contractors at Moor Marketing Agency who are not meeting performance expectations in their assigned role.

## 1. Identifying Underperformance

### 1.1 Common Indicators

- 
Missed deadlines or deliverables

- 
Low-quality work or repeated errors

- 
Poor communication or lack of collaboration

- 
Failure to adhere to SOPs, tools (e.g., [Monday.com](http://Monday.com), Slack), or time tracking

- 
Inability to meet role-based KPIs

### 1.2 Responsibility

- 
**Line Managers** or **Project Leads** are responsible for observing, documenting, and initiating discussions around underperformance.

## 2. Initial Informal Discussion

### 2.1 Private Meeting

- 
The line manager arranges a **one-on-one meeting** with the team member.

- 
Purpose: Raise concerns, allow the team member to respond, and understand any underlying issues.

### 2.2 Key Actions

- 
Outline specific examples of underperformance.

- 
Listen to the team member’s perspective.

- 
Discuss any challenges or barriers to performance.

- 
Reaffirm expectations and offer initial support.

📌 *If improvement occurs after the informal chat, no further action may be needed. If concerns persist, proceed to the formal process.*

## 3. Formal Performance Management Plan (PMP)

### 3.1 Meeting to Initiate Plan

- 
A formal meeting is scheduled with:

- 
The team member

- 
Their line manager

- 
A member of HR (if applicable)

### 3.2 Documentation

- 
A **Performance Management Plan (PMP)** is presented and signed. It must include:

- 
**Summary of Issues**: Clear, specific examples of underperformance

- 
**Performance Goals**: Defined and measurable KPIs the team member is expected to meet

- 
**Support Measures**: Training, mentorship, tools, or changes to help the team member succeed

- 
**Monitoring Period**: Typically 2–4 weeks, depending on the severity and complexity

- 
**Review Schedule**: Weekly or fortnightly check-ins during the period

## 4. Monitoring & Support

### 4.1 Regular Check-Ins

- 
Check-ins are held at agreed intervals to:

- 
Review progress toward KPIs

- 
Provide constructive feedback

- 
Document progress and challenges

- 
Adjust support measures if needed

### 4.2 Documentation

- 
Each check-in is documented and shared with the team member.

- 
Progress is recorded in a shared and confidential file (e.g., HR folder in SharePoint).

## 5. End-of-Plan Review

### 5.1 Outcomes

At the end of the review period, the manager will assess performance against the agreed KPIs. Possible outcomes include:

- 
**Improved Performance**: Team member meets expectations and is returned to regular duties.

- 
**Partial Improvement**: A short extension of the PMP with adjusted KPIs may be granted.

- 
**No Improvement**: The agency may proceed with further HR action, which could include role reassignment, final warning, or termination, in line with workplace laws and contractual obligations.

## 6. Confidentiality & Conduct

- 
All discussions and documentation are to remain confidential.

- 
The process must be handled professionally and respectfully, maintaining the dignity of all parties involved.

# Data & File Management

📁 Moor Marketing Agency SOP: Utilizing SharePoint for Client File Storage

## Purpose

To establish a standardised method for organising, storing, and accessing client-related documents within SharePoint, ensuring consistency, ease of access, and collaboration across all teams.

## Scope

This SOP applies to all team members involved in creating, managing, and accessing client files within the SharePoint environment.

## Folder Structure

For each client, create a dedicated folder within the SharePoint "Clients" document library. Inside each client folder, maintain the following standardized subfolders:

- 
**Proposal**: Store all proposal documents, including initial drafts and final versions.

- 
**Videos**: Upload all video content related to the client, such as advertisements, testimonials, and project recordings.

- 
**Images**: Save all image assets, including logos, graphics, and photographs.

- 
**Client Shared Folder**: Use this folder for documents and files that are shared directly with the client. Ensure only appropriate content is placed here.

- 
**Reporting**: Maintain all reports, analytics, and performance metrics related to the client's projects.

- 
**Strategy**: Document all strategic plans, meeting notes, and brainstorming sessions pertaining to the client's marketing [approach.convergepoint.com](http://approach.convergepoint.com)

## Procedures

### 1. Creating a New Client Folder

- 
Navigate to the "Clients" document library in SharePoint.

- 
Click on "New Folder" and name it using the client's official name (e.g., "Acme Corp").

- 
Within the newly created client folder, create the six standardized subfolders listed above

### 2. Uploading and Managing Files

- 
Ensure all files are uploaded to the appropriate subfolder.

- 
Use clear and descriptive file names, including dates and version numbers where applicable (e.g., "Acme_Proposal_2025-05-25_v1.docx").

- 
Avoid storing files in the root of the client folder; always place them in the relevant subfolder.

### 3. Access and Permissions

- 
Set permissions at the client folder level to restrict access to authorized team members only.

- 
For the "Client Shared Folder," ensure permissions are configured to allow client access while maintaining security protocols.

- 
Regularly review and update permissions to reflect team changes.

### 4. Version Control

- 
Utilise SharePoint's version history feature to track changes to documents.

- 
Before making significant edits, check out the document to prevent conflicts.

- 
After edits, check the document back in and add a comment summarizing the changes made.

### 5. Maintenance and Review

- 
Conduct quarterly reviews of each client folder to archive outdated materials and ensure current documents are up to date.

- 
Remove duplicate or unnecessary files to maintain organization.

- 
Update folder structures as needed to accommodate new types of content or changes in project scope.

## Best Practices

- 
Keep folder and file names concise and consistent.

- 
Avoid deep nesting of folders to simplify navigation.

- 
Utilize metadata and tags to enhance searchability within SharePoint.

- 
Provide training sessions for new team members on SharePoint usage and this SOP

# How to Create SOP's

How to Create SOPs in Your Agency: A Practical Guide

Creating SOPs doesn't have to be complicated. Think of it as capturing the way you and your team work, so everyone stays aligned and tasks are completed consistently. Here's how to do it step by step.

## 1. Identify Key Processes

Start by listing the tasks you and your team perform regularly. Focus on those that are:

- 
Repetitive

- 
Time-consuming

- 
Prone to errors

- 
Critical for client satisfaction

These are prime candidates for SOPs.

Use the task dump worksheet or this 

## 2. Record the Process

Instead of writing everything down from scratch, record yourself or a team member performing the task. Use screen recording tools like Loom or Zoom to capture the process in real-time. Narrate each step as you go, explaining what you're doing and why.

## 3. Transcribe the Recording

Once you have the recording, transcribe it to create a written version of the process. Tools like [Otter.ai](http://otter.ai/) or Descript can help with this. Having a transcript allows team members who prefer reading over watching videos to understand the process clearly.

## 4. Create a Step-by-Step Guide

Using the transcript, outline the process in clear, numbered steps. Keep it simple and concise. For example:

- 
Open the project management tool.

- 
Navigate to the current project.

- 
Update the task status to "In Progress."

This format makes it easy for anyone to follow.

## 5. Store and Share the SOP

Save the SOP in a centralized location accessible to your team, such as a shared drive or a documentation tool like Notion or Confluence. Make sure it's organized logically, so team members can find what they need quickly.

## 6. Review and Update Regularly

Processes can change over time. Schedule regular reviews of your SOPs to ensure they remain accurate and relevant. Encourage team members to suggest updates when they notice discrepancies or improvements.

title: Daily Mindset Ritual: Rewire for Success

# Daily Mindset Ritual: Rewire for Success

### **Daily Mindset Ritual: Rewire for Success**

**Purpose:**
This ritual is designed to help you reprogram your subconscious mind to align with your goals, boost your confidence, and reinforce your value. Success is an identity before it’s a result—this daily practice helps you step into that identity.

**Step 1: Morning Goal Affirmation (Repeat x3)**

Start your day by speaking your primary goals out loud **three times** in this format:

"I am so happy and grateful now that I have attracted [your goal]."

Examples:

- 
"I am so happy and grateful now that I have attracted five aligned, high-ticket clients."

- 
"I am so happy and grateful now that I have created a thriving business doing what I love."

Speak slowly, with emotion, and visualize each goal as already done.

**Step 2: "I Am" Mantras (5–10 minutes)**

Engage in "I Am" affirmations that speak directly to your **value, power, and identity**. You can:

- 
Use your own recorded voice

- 
Read from a list or book of affirmations

- 
Listen to a guided audio or mantra track (YouTube, Insight Timer, Spotify, etc.)

Examples:

- 
"I am valuable."

- 
"I am worthy of abundance."

- 
"I am magnetic to success."

- 
"I am a powerful creator."

Feel the words as truths. These are not just affirmations—they are **identity statements**.

**Why This Matters:**

Your **subconscious mind** does not differentiate between imagination and reality—it simply responds to repetition and emotion. By **repeating your goals** and affirming your value each day, you're:

- 
Rewiring your beliefs about what's possible

- 
Reinforcing that you are worthy of success

- 
Aligning your inner state with the outcomes you’re creating

When your **subconscious beliefs** support your goals, execution becomes smoother, faster, and more intuitive.

title: The Perfect Day Excercise
body:
# The Perfect Day Excercise

## 📋 The Perfect Day Exercise: A Step-by-Step Guide

### 1️⃣ **Set the Scene**

Before you begin writing, find a quiet, comfortable place where you can focus without distractions. Gather a notebook or journal, and set aside at least 30 minutes to complete the exercise.

**Tip:** Some people prefer to do this exercise in the morning with a clear mind, while others find it easier in the evening when they can reflect on the day.

### 2️⃣ **Define the Purpose**

Take a moment to understand why you’re doing this exercise:

- 
To gain clarity on what truly matters to you.

- 
To set meaningful goals and align your actions with your values.

- 
To create a roadmap that motivates you to build the life you want.

Write a short statement in your journal about why this exercise matters to you. For example:

“I’m doing this exercise to understand what a fulfilling day looks like for me, so I can start making choices that align with that vision.”

### 3️⃣ **Visualize Your Ideal Day**

Close your eyes, take a few deep breaths, and imagine your perfect day from the moment you wake up to the moment you go to sleep. Focus on the details:

- 
**Where are you?** (Home, a villa in Bali, a city loft?)

- 
**Who are you with?** (Family, partner, friends, alone?)

- 
**What are you doing?** (Work, hobbies, exercise, social activities?)

- 
**How do you feel?** (Energetic, relaxed, inspired?)

- 
**What does your environment look like?** (Colors, sounds, smells?)

Let your imagination run free—don’t worry about practicality or constraints yet.

### 4️⃣ **Write It Out in Detail**

Now, write your perfect day as a **narrative**, describing it in the present tense as if it’s happening right now. For example:

“I wake up naturally at 6:30 a.m. feeling refreshed. Sunlight filters through the curtains of my peaceful bedroom. I stretch, feeling grateful for the day ahead. I walk into the kitchen, where the aroma of fresh coffee greets me...”

**Include:**

- 
**Morning routine:** How do you start your day? What energizes you?

- 
**Midday:** What activities fill your day? What work or hobbies excite you?

- 
**Evening:** How do you wind down? Who do you spend time with?

- 
**Emotions and sensations:** How do you feel at each stage of the day?

Aim for **1-3 pages** to capture enough detail.

### 5️⃣ **Reflect and Extract Key Themes**

After writing, read your narrative slowly. Ask yourself:

- 
What themes emerge? (Freedom, creativity, connection, purpose?)

- 
What values stand out? (Family, adventure, contribution?)

- 
Which parts excite you most?

Highlight or underline these key elements. They’ll guide you in setting goals and priorities.

### 6️⃣ **Identify Action Steps**

Look at your perfect day and identify **one or two small steps** you can take right now to move toward that vision. For example:

- 
If your perfect day includes exercise, schedule a morning walk.

- 
If it includes meaningful work, research new career paths or projects.

Write these steps in your journal and commit to taking action.

## 🔄 **Repeat Regularly**

Revisit this exercise every 6-12 months (or whenever you feel stuck) to see how your vision evolves. It’s normal for your perfect day to change as you grow.

## ✨ Final Tips

- 
**Be honest:** Don’t write what you *think* your day should look like; write what truly excites and fulfills you.

- 
**Avoid judgment:** Let go of guilt or limitations. Dream big!

- 
**Use sensory details:** The more vivid the narrative, the more powerful the exercise.

title: Upwork Hiring Guide
body:
# Upwork Hiring Guide

🧭 Upwork Hiring Guide: Find and Hire Top Freelancers with Confidence

This guide walks you through each stage of hiring on Upwork—from preparing your brief to making a confident hire and setting up for success.

Sample Job Post 👉 [Access Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MhoEXOBVPlsIxmQi52F3LvknXWWOYO_Nkntf8PFVi8o/edit?usp=sharing)

## ✅ 1. **Get Clear on What You Need**

Before posting any job, define the following:

### 🛠 Project Scope

- 
What is the deliverable? (e.g., website design, sales page, video editing)

- 
Is this a one-time project or ongoing work?

- 
What skills are non-negotiable?

### 📅 Timeline

- 
When do you need the work delivered?

- 
Is there a fixed deadline or flexibility?

### 💰 Budget

- 
Set a budget range based on project complexity

- 
Decide: **hourly** (great for ongoing tasks) vs. **fixed-price** (best for defined deliverables)

## 📝 2. **Write a High-Quality Job Post**

A clear, specific job post attracts top talent.

### 🧱 Include:

- 
A strong title (e.g., “Experienced Brand Designer Needed for Website Redesign”)

- 
A detailed project description

- 
Required skills and tools (e.g., Figma, Webflow, SEMrush)

- 
Your expectations: turnaround time, communication style, deliverables

- 
Bonus if: you include links, examples, or a creative brief

## 🧲 3. **Set Filters to Attract the Right Freelancers**

When posting the job, set smart filters:

- 
**Talent Type**: Freelancer vs. Agency

- 
**Experience Level**: Entry, Intermediate, or Expert

- 
**Location** (optional): Ideal if you want to align time zones or cultural fluency

- 
**English Proficiency**: Set this depending on the communication level required

## 🔎 4. **Review Applicants Strategically**

Focus on:

- 
**Portfolio relevance**: Do their past projects match your needs?

- 
**Proposal quality**: Is it personalized and thoughtful, or copy-paste?

- 
**Reviews & ratings**: Read client feedback and check for consistency

- 
**Test project** (optional): Use a paid micro-task to validate their ability

## 💬 5. **Interview the Shortlist**

Use video or chat to clarify:

- 
Their approach to your project

- 
Availability and timezone

- 
Communication expectations (response time, channels)

- 
Ask scenario-based or technical questions relevant to the task

## ✍️ 6. **Make the Offer**

When you’re confident:

- 
**Send the offer** via Upwork’s platform (hourly or fixed)

- 
Define clear **milestones** for fixed-price projects

- 
Reiterate expectations in the **contract notes**

## 🚀 7. **Set Up for a Successful Engagement**

- 
**Kickoff message or call**: Clarify goals, workflow, and tools

- 
Share necessary files, logins, or SOPs

- 
Use tools like Slack, Trello, Loom, or Notion for streamlined collaboration

## 🧠 Bonus Tips for Hiring Success

- 
**Always test with a small project first** before committing long-term

- 
Use Loom to record briefs—it saves time and avoids miscommunication

- 
Pay fairly—great freelancers are an investment, not a cost

- 
Leave honest reviews—this improves Upwork for everyone

title: How to Build SOP's
body:
# How to Build SOP's

How to Create SOPs in Your Agency: A Practical Guide

Creating SOPs doesn't have to be complicated. Think of it as capturing the way you and your team work, so everyone stays aligned and tasks are completed consistently. Here's how to do it step by step.

## 1. Identify Key Processes

Start by listing the tasks you and your team perform regularly. Focus on those that are:

- 
Repetitive

- 
Time-consuming

- 
Prone to errors

- 
Critical for client satisfaction

These are prime candidates for SOPs.

Use the task dump worksheet or this 

## 2. Record the Process

Instead of writing everything down from scratch, record yourself or a team member performing the task. Use screen recording tools like Loom or Zoom to capture the process in real-time. Narrate each step as you go, explaining what you're doing and why.

## 3. Transcribe the Recording

Once you have the recording, transcribe it to create a written version of the process. Tools like [Otter.ai](http://Otter.ai) or Descript can help with this. Having a transcript allows team members who prefer reading over watching videos to understand the process clearly.

## 4. Create a Step-by-Step Guide

Using the transcript, outline the process in clear, numbered steps. Keep it simple and concise. For example:

- 
Open the project management tool.

- 
Navigate to the current project.

- 
Update the task status to "In Progress."

This format makes it easy for anyone to follow.

## 5. Store and Share the SOP

Save the SOP in a centralized location accessible to your team, such as a shared drive or a documentation tool like Notion or Confluence. Make sure it's organized logically, so team members can find what they need quickly.

## 6. Review and Update Regularly

Processes can change over time. Schedule regular reviews of your SOPs to ensure they remain accurate and relevant. Encourage team members to suggest updates when they notice discrepancies or improvements.

# Step 9: Facebook Ad Structure & Setup

## 🎯 Facebook Ads Setup Guide for Case Study Funnels

This guide will help you run **high-quality, conversion-focused Facebook ads** — especially for service-based offers, coaching programs, or agency retainers.

## 🧠 STEP 1: Define the Campaign Strategy

### ✳️ Objective:

- 
Use **“Conversions”** or **“Leads”** depending on your funnel type:

- 
If sending to a landing page → **Conversions (opt for “Schedule” or “Lead” as event)**

- 
If using native Facebook Lead Forms → **Leads objective** (⚠️ lower quality)

## 🧍 STEP 2: Targeting Settings

### 🎯 **Audience Niche**

![image](https://assets-v2.circle.so/jl7rx0pgmz31bhjkbct22aawjm2a)

**Pro Tip:** Stack interests to test different angles — don’t mix totally unrelated interests in one ad set.

### 👥 **Age & Gender**

- 
Start with **25–45**, expand if needed.

- 
If your ideal client skews heavily one way, **split by gender in separate ad sets** to test.

## 💰 STEP 3: Budget Structure - Test with ABO First

### ➤ **ABO (Ad Set Budget Optimization):**

- 
Start with 3–5 ad sets (different audiences).

- 
Set budget at ad set level (e.g. $20–$50/day per set).

This gives you **control over spend per audience**, making it easier to identify winners early.

### 🔁 **Switch Winning Audiences to CBO:**

Once you see 1–2 ad sets converting:

- 
Create a new **CBO (Campaign Budget Optimization)** campaign.

- 
Put only **your top performers** in here.

- 
Let Facebook optimize across them automatically.

## 📍 STEP 4: Placement Settings

- 
Choose **Manual Placements**

- 
**Select ONLY:**

- 
**Facebook Feed**

- 
**Instagram Feed**

- 
**Instagram Stories (optional if story creative exists)**

- 
**Facebook Stories (optional)**

**Uncheck**:

- 
Audience Network

- 
Messenger

- 
In-article / Reels (unless testing specifically for mobile video)

This keeps your budget focused on high-intent placements.

## 🚫 STEP 5: Exclude Leads

To avoid wasting budget on people who already opted in:

### How:

- 
In **Ad Set > Exclude Audience**, select:

- 
Custom Audience of existing leads (email list or lead pixel event)

- 
Website visitors who saw your thank you page

- 
Booked call custom conversion (if set up)

**Tip:** If you don’t have this yet, build as soon as you get 100+ leads.

## 🧪 STEP 6: Ad Creative & Copy

- 
Use video testimonials, case study highlights, or bold transformation statements.

- 
Include a clear **Call to Action**: “Watch the Case Study” → “Book a Call”

- 
Use **1x Primary Text**, **1x Headline**, and a **‘Learn More’** CTA button

## ⚠️ Notes on Lead Ads

You *can* use **Lead Ads (native forms)** for lower friction and cheaper leads.

BUT:

- 
Expect lower quality — people may not even remember opting in.

- 
Great for volume, but you’ll need **strong nurture** post-lead (SMS/email automations).

- 
Best used with retargeting or as a secondary strategy.

## 🧩 Optional: Retargeting Campaign

Once you get volume, set up a **warm retargeting campaign**:

- 
Audience: Page viewers, 75%+ video viewers, engagers, email list

- 
Creative: Testimonials, credibility-building content

- 
Budget: 10–20% of your daily spend

title: Step 2: Prepare Copy
body:
# Step 2: Prepare Copy

You will need (you can see the layout in the landing page guide)

1. **Headline (Results-Focused)**

Hook with the outcome, not the service.

*Example:* “How We Helped The Retail Co. Increase Ecommerce Sales by 212% in 90 Days Without Paid Ads”

**Tips:**

- 
Focus on results and timeframe.

- 
Avoid jargon — make it instantly clear what changed.

### **2. Client Overview**

Provide brief context so readers understand who the client is.

*Example:* “Retail Co. is a mid-sized fashion brand with a Shopify store and a small internal marketing team.”

**Include:**

- 
Industry

- 
Size / stage

- 
What they were struggling with

### **3. The Challenge**

Describe what wasn’t working.

*Prompt:* “Before working with us, [client] was struggling with…”

**Goal:** Make your ideal prospect nod along — they should see *themselves* in this problem.

### **4. The Solution / Your Approach**

Detail how you helped, step by step.

- 
What was your process?

- 
What did you prioritize?

- 
What was unique about your approach?

**Bonus:** Use this section to embed your framework or IP.

### **5. The Results**

Be specific and quantifiable.

*Example:* “Sales increased by 212%, returning customers grew by 37%, and conversion rate improved from 1.2% to 3.8%.”

**Include:**

- 
Before/after stats

- 
Screenshots or graphs

- 
Client quotes backing the results

### **6. Testimonial or Client Quote**

Let the client speak.

*Prompt them:* “What was it like working with us?” “What surprised you most?” “Would you recommend us?”

**Format Tip:** Use bold pull quotes for emphasis.

### **7. Call to Action**

End with a prompt to engage.

- 
“Want similar results? Book a free audit.”

- 
“Curious how this would apply to your brand? Let’s talk.”

**Link to:** your sales page, calendar

title: Step 3: Generate Client Testimonial
body:
# Step 3: Generate Client Testimonial

Text testimonials are useful, but **video adds authenticity**, body language, and emotion. They humanize your results and help prospective clients say, “I trust this person.”

Video testimonials are:

- 
More believable

- 
More engaging

- 
Easier to repurpose on socials, websites, sales pages, and proposals

## ✅ The Testimonial Formula (Simple, Story-Driven)

When requesting testimonial videos, guide your clients through this 3-part story arc:

### **1. The Problem**

*“What were you struggling with before working with us?”*

Encourage specifics. You want future prospects to recognize themselves in this.

### **2. The Turning Point**

*“Why wasn’t what you tried working?”*
*“What made you decide to get help?”*

This helps show how they looked for a solution but couldn’t solve it alone — positioning your offer as the key.

### **3. The Solution & Why It Worked**

*“What changed once we started working together?”*
*“What surprised you about the experience?”*
*“Why do you think it worked so well?”*

This is where they share the actual transformation and highlight the value of your specific method, not just the result.

Example:

[https://youtu.be/_0r-_jrnjFU?si=ov2ncLfMJB_uWpIw](https://youtu.be/_0r-_jrnjFU?si=ov2ncLfMJB_uWpIw)

CTA above the fold

Working form/buttons

Clear headline and benefits

Branded fonts/colors

title: Step 7: Create Email Nurture
body:
# Step 7: Create Email Nurture

## ✉️ Pre-Call Nurture Email Sequence (3–5 Emails)

Each email has a **goal**, suggested **timing**, and **sample copy** you can tailor.

### ✅ **Email 1: Confirmation & Excitement**

**When:** Immediately after booking
**Goal:** Confirm, affirm their decision, and set expectations

**Subject:** You’re all booked in here’s what to expect 🙌
**Body:**

Hey [Name],

You’re officially booked in for our call on **[DATE/TIME]**.

I’m genuinely excited to connect, whether you’re feeling stuck, scaling fast, or somewhere in between, this session is designed to give you clarity, not a sales pitch.

In the meantime, here’s what we’ll cover:

- 
Where you're at

- 
What’s working / what’s not

- 
A roadmap to move forward

**Quick tip:** Bring any questions or challenges you’re facing; this is your time!

Chat soon,
**[Your Name]**

### ✅ **Email 2: Authority + Relevance**

**When:** 1–2 days after booking
**Goal:** Build credibility, show others like them have succeeded with you

**Subject:** How [Client Name] went from [Before] to [After]
**Body:**

Hey [Name],

Thought I’d share a quick story [Client Name] was in a similar spot to you: [brief pain point].

We worked together to [1–2 sentence description of the transformation]. Within [timeframe], they saw [specific result].

Why am I sharing this? Because you’re not alone. And what you want *is* possible with the right plan.

More stories like this: [Link to case study page or video testimonial]

Speak soon,
**[Your Name]**

### ✅ **Email 3: Pre-Frame the Call**

**When:** 1–2 days before the call
**Goal:** Reduce resistance, frame the value, reduce no-shows

**Subject:** What to expect from our call (and what not to)
**Body:**

Hey [Name],

Just a quick note before our call. This isn’t a sales trap or a pitch deck.

Instead, you’ll leave with:
✅ Clarity on what’s keeping you stuck
✅ A roadmap tailored to your stage
✅ (If it’s a fit) how I can help

You’ll *never* be pressured, I’m here to serve, not convince.

Looking forward to connecting on **[DATE/TIME]**. If anything changes, just hit reply.

 [Your Name]

### 🧠 Optional Email 4: Resource Boost

**When:** Day before or morning of the call
**Goal:** Warm them up with value so they show up already primed

**Subject:** Thought this might help before we chat
**Body:**

Hey [Name],

Since we’ll be diving into [topic/area], here’s a quick resource you might find helpful:

→ [Link to a relevant blog post, video, framework, etc.]

It gives a great overview of [concept / myth / mistake you’ll help them avoid].

Looking forward to helping you map out the next steps.

See you soon!
**[Your Name]**

### ✅ **Email 5: Same-Day Reminder (Short & Human)**

**When:** Morning of the call
**Goal:** Friendly reminder to reduce no-shows

**Subject:** Still good for today?
**Body:**

Just a quick check, still good for our call at **[TIME]** today?

Can’t wait to dive in. Bring anything you’ve been stuck on.

[Your Name]

# Step 8: Pixel Setup

## 🛠️ Step-by-Step: Creating Your Facebook Pixel

### **1. Go to Meta Events Manager**

- 
Visit: [https://business.facebook.com/events_manager](https://business.facebook.com/events_manager)

- 
Select your **Business Manager Account**.

### **2. Create a New Pixel**

- 
Click **“+ Connect Data Sources”** → Choose **Web**.

- 
Select **Meta Pixel** → Click **Connect**.

- 
Name your Pixel (e.g. “Case Study Funnel Pixel”).

- 
Enter your website URL and click **Continue**.

## 🔧 Step 3: Add the Pixel to Your Website

You have 3 options:

### a) **Using a Platform (e.g. WordPress, Shopify, Kajabi)**

- 
Use native integrations or plugins (e.g. Facebook for WordPress).

- 
Paste your Pixel ID (not the full code) where prompted.

### b) **Manual Install**

- 
Copy the base pixel code.

- 
Paste it **in the <head> section** of all funnel pages (Landing, Case Study, Booking Page, Thank You).

### c) **Use Google Tag Manager**

- 
Create a new tag.

- 
Paste the pixel code.

- 
Trigger it to fire on all pages or specific URLs.

## 🎯 Step 4: Track Key Events in Your Funnel

You’ll want to set up **standard events** and optionally **custom events**:

![image](https://assets-v2.circle.so/gjb8qb9utif619x4qgu1g2b0jftx)

### **How to Set Up Events**

- 
Use **Event Setup Tool** in Events Manager to point-and-click.

- 
OR use **manual code**: Add fbq('track', 'EventName'); where needed.

## 🧪 Step 5: Test Your Pixel

Use the **Meta Pixel Helper Chrome Extension** to:

- 
Check if the pixel is firing on each funnel step

- 
Confirm correct event names

- 
Troubleshoot any issues

## 🔁 Step 6: Build Audiences (Optional but Powerful)

Inside **Ads Manager** → **Audiences**:

- 
**Case Study Viewers** → Retarget with follow-up testimonials or a “You forgot to book” message.

- 
**Booked Calls** → Exclude from future ads.

- 
**Lookalike of Bookers** → For prospecting cold traffic.

## ✅ Best Practices

- 
**Use URL-based rules** if you’re not using event code (e.g. “contains /thank-you”).

- 
**Name your events and audiences clearly** (e.g. “CaseStudy_ViewContent_June2025”).

- 
**Set up custom conversions** if your funnel platform doesn’t allow granular event code.

# Instagram Outreach

## 📸 The Power of Instagram Cold Outreach

- 
**Direct Access to Decision-Makers**: Instagram allows you to engage directly with business owners and decision-makers, often bypassing traditional gatekeepers.

- 
**High Engagement Rates**: Compared to other channels like email, Instagram DMs often yield higher open and response rates, facilitating more meaningful interactions. 

- 
**Visual Platform Advantage**: The visual nature of Instagram enables you to showcase your agency's work, making your outreach more compelling.

## ⏱️ Expected Response Time

- 
**Initial Responses**: Many prospects respond within 24 to 72 hours of receiving a well-crafted DM.

- 
**Follow-Ups**: If there's no response initially, sending a follow-up message after a few days can increase the likelihood of engagement.

## ✅ Pros of Instagram Cold Outreach

- 
**Personalized Communication**: Tailored messages can resonate more with recipients, leading to higher engagement.

- 
**Cost-Effective**: Reaching out via DMs eliminates the need for ad spend, making it a budget-friendly 

- 
**Scalable with Automation**: Tools like DMPro and ColdDMs can help automate and scale your outreach efforts efficiently. 

## ❌ Cons of Instagram Cold Outreach

- 
**Platform Limitations**: Instagram imposes daily limits on the number of DMs you can send, which can restrict outreach volume.

- 
**Risk of Being Marked as Spam**: Overly generic or frequent messages can lead to your account being flagged or restricted. Make sure you also limit requests to 10-20 a day.

**Time-Consuming**: Crafting personalized messages and managing conversations can be labor-intensive without automation tools.

title: The Lead Ecosystem
body:
# The Lead Ecosystem

![image](https://assets-v2.circle.so/pztfgpaste4108iqu3dqo80qwifk)

This module provides a structured approach to understanding and implementing a lead generation ecosystem. You'll learn how to set up, measure, and optimize your lead generation funnel by establishing benchmarks tailored to your agency's unique goals and operations.

### 1. 🌐 Understanding the Lead Generation Ecosystem

The lead generation ecosystem encompasses all the strategies, tools, and processes used to attract and convert potential clients. It's a dynamic system that requires continuous monitoring and optimization.

### 2. 🧱 Building the Foundation

- 
**Define Your Ideal Client Profile (ICP)**: Identify the characteristics of clients who benefit most from your services

- 
**Develop a Value Proposition**: Clearly articulate the unique value your agency offers.

- 
**Set Goals & Financial**: Establish Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound objectives for your lead generation

### 3. 📊 Establishing Benchmarks

Setting internal benchmarks is crucial for measuring success and identifying areas for improvement.

- 
**Cost Per Lead (CPL)**: Determine the average cost to acquire a lead through each channel.

- 
**Conversion Rates**: Measure the percentage of leads that convert into clients.

- 
**Lead Velocity**: Track the speed at which leads move through your sales funnel.

### 4. 📣 Channel Strategies

- 
Inbound Lead Acquisition Strategies (Content, SEO, Social Media, Webinars)

- 
Outbound Lead Acquisition Strategies: Cold emailing, LinkedIn, Instagram, Lumpy Mail

- 
Paid Advertising Strategies: Facebook & Instagram, Display

- 
Partnerships: White label, Referral

- 
Community & Networking: Online communities, local networking, public speaking, hosting workshops

### 5. 🔄 Nurturing Leads

Not all leads will convert immediately. Implement nurturing strategies to keep your agency top-of-mind:

- 
**Email Campaigns**: Send regular newsletters with valuable content.

- 
**Retargeting Ads**: Use ads to re-engage visitors who didn't convert.

- 
**Webinars and Workshops**: Offer free sessions to provide value and showcase expertise.

### 6. 📈 Monitoring and Optimization

Regularly review your lead generation metrics to identify what's working and what needs adjustment.

- 
**A/B Testing**: Test different messages, landing pages, and offers to see what resonates best.

- 
**Feedback Loops**: Gather feedback from leads and clients to refine your approach.

- 
**Continuous Learning**: Stay updated with the latest trends and tools in lead generation.

### 7. 🛠 Tools and Resources

- 
**CRM Systems**: Manage and track interactions with leads.

- 
**Analytics Platforms**: Monitor website traffic and user behavior.

- 
**Automation Tools**: Streamline outreach and follow-up processes.

### Conclusion

Building a robust lead generation ecosystem requires a strategic approach, continuous monitoring, and adaptability. By setting clear benchmarks and leveraging the right channels and tools, agency owners can create a sustainable system that consistently attracts and converts high-quality leads.

If you need assistance in creating customized templates or dashboards to track these metrics, feel free to ask!

# Step 4. Funnel Creation

## 🚀 How to Set Up a LinkedIn Campaign in Dripify

### 1. **Sign Up and Connect Your LinkedIn Account**

- 
**Create a Dripify Account**: Visit [Dripify's website](https://dripify.io/) and sign up for an account.

- 
**Connect LinkedIn**: After signing up, link your LinkedIn account to Dripify. This integration allows Dripify to perform actions on your behalf, such as sending connection requests and messages. 

### 2. **Add Leads to Your Campaign**

- 
**Using LinkedIn Search**:

- 
Perform a targeted search on LinkedIn to find potential leads.

- 
Copy the URL of the search results page.

- 
In Dripify, create a new lead list and paste the copied URL.

- 
Specify the number of leads you want to add from this search. 

- 
**Uploading a CSV File**:

- 
Prepare a CSV file containing LinkedIn profile URLs of your target leads.

- 
In Dripify, choose the option to upload leads via CSV and import your 

### 3. **Create a Campaign Sequence**

- 
**Start a New Campaign**: Click on "Create New Campaign" in your Dripify 

- 
**Choose or Build a Sequence**:

- 
Select a pre-built template or create a custom sequence tailored to your outreach goals.

- 
Common actions include:

- 
Viewing a profile

- 
Sending a connection request (with or without a message)

- 
Following up with messages after connection acceptance

- 
Endorsing skills or liking posts

- 
**Set Delays and Conditions**:

- 
Introduce delays between actions to mimic natural behavior.

- 
Use conditions to branch your sequence based on lead responses (e.g., if a lead replies, send a specific follow-up message).

### 4. **Customize Your Messages**

- 
**Personalize Content**:

- 
Use dynamic placeholders like {First Name}, {Company}, or {Job Title} to tailor messages to each lead.

- 
Craft messages that are concise, relevant, and value-driven

- 
**Alternative Messages**:

- 
Prepare fallback messages for leads with missing information to ensure continuity in your outreach.

### 5. **Set Campaign Parameters**

- 
**Name Your Campaign**: Assign a descriptive name to easily identify your campaign.

- 
**Define Skipping Criteria**:

- 
Set rules to skip certain profiles, such as those without profile pictures or specific keywords.

- 
**Integrate with Other Tools**:

- 
Connect Dripify with platforms like Zapier, HubSpot, or Google Sheets to automate data flow and enhance functionality.

### 6. **Launch and Monitor Your Campaign**

- 
**Start the Campaign**: Review all settings and initiate the campaign

- 
**Monitor Performance**:

- 
Use Dripify's analytics dashboard to track metrics such as connection request acceptance rates, message replies, and overall engagement.

- 
Adjust your sequence or messaging based on performance data to optimize results

title: Domain Deliverability Setup
body:
# Domain Deliverability Setup

**SEQUENCE:**

- 
Connect your domain to your sending tool (Mailshake Instanly, Smartlead, lemlist, Lusha).

- 
Set up SPF.

- 
Set up DKIM.

- 
Publish DMARC (start with “none” mode).

- 
Wait 24 to 48 hours before sending.

**SETUP SPF**

How to set it up (search SPF for your email provider)

- 
Your sending tool will show something like:

- 
Type: TXT

- 
Name: @

- 
Value: v=spf1 include:[instanlymail.com](http://instanlymail.com) include:_[spf.google.com](http://spf.google.com) ~all

(Example only. Yours may differ.)

Steps:

- 
Log in to your domain registrar (GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudflare, Google Domains).

- 
Go to DNS Settings or DNS Zone.

- 
Click “Add Record”

- 
Choose TXT

- 
Paste the exact SPF value from your sending tool

- 
Save

Important rule:

One domain must only have one SPF record.

If you already have one, you combine them instead of creating a second one.

**SETUP DKIM**

Type: TXT

Name: something like

selector._domainkey

Value: a long string of characters (your DKIM key)

Steps:

- 
In your DNS panel, click “Add Record”

- 
Select TXT

- 
Paste DKIM Name

- 
Paste DKIM Value

- 
Save

Your sending tool will mark DKIM as “verified” once it detects the record.

**SETUP DMARC**

DMARC record (you can copy this)

- 
Type: TXT

- 
Name: _dmarc

- 
Value:

- 
v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=[mailto:your-email@yourdomain.com](mailto:your-email@yourdomain.com); ruf=[mailto:your-email@yourdomain.com](mailto:your-email@yourdomain.com); pct=100

- 
Replace “[your-email@yourdomain.com](mailto:your-email@yourdomain.com)” with your real monitored inbox.

Steps:

- 
Click “Add Record”

- 
Choose TXT

- 
Name: _dmarc

- 
Paste the DMARC value above

- 
Save

DMARC will start monitoring within 24 hours.
